intended_object: The relative norm (trace/corestriction map) N_{U/V} : A^V → A^U, x ↦ Σ_{t ∈ U/V} t·x, for open normal subgroups V ≤ U, restricted to the chosen coefficient submodules M_V → M_U of a restricted level system. Inferred from the docstring and the structure `RestrictedLevelSystem`, whose field `relativeNorm_mem` says the relative norm maps M_V into M_U.
explanation:
The body applies the library's `LevelCompact.relativeNorm A U V h` to the underlying element of x ∈ M_V and packages the result as an element of M_U, using the field `S.relativeNorm_mem`. Additivity and R-linearity follow from those of the ambient map. So it is the ambient relative norm (a sum over a right transversal of V in U; the library proves it does not depend on the transversal) restricted to the chosen submodules, which is exactly what the docstring says.

The map is in effect Mathlib's general `LinearMap.restrict`, written out by hand for this map. That is a packaging choice, not a missing generalization: no separate Mathlib notion of this restricted norm exists.

The restriction to open normal subgroups is not a narrowing of generality. The coefficient system is indexed by open normal levels by design: each level carries a residual G/U-representation. The surrounding hypotheses (compact topological group, `Rep R G`) are the setting of the whole development. The definition is correct and at the right generality.
